deals.loanType: Fixed-rate portfolio loan, 5 years interest-only then amortizing
deals.debtPrepay: Prior to the 7th loan year: yield maintenance. 7th to 8th loan year: 2.0% of principal prepaid. 8th to 9th loan year: 1.0% of principal prepaid. After the 9th loan year: no fee.
deals.debtNotes: Brickyard Plaza is one of NINE assets encumbered by a single $100,441,000 Guggenheim Real Estate loan (Oct-2022 origination, 5.25% fixed, matures Nov-2032, 5 years IO then amortizing, estimated Year 1 NOI across the nine assets of $13,580,000). The other eight are Fairview Commons, Gold Star Plaza, Golden Triangle, Hamburg Square, Pine Grove Plaza, Southington Center, Trexler Mall and Washington Center Shoppes. The $14,749,120 shown here is Brickyard's allocated balance, not a standalone loan. Release is permitted on sale to a non-affiliate subject to a release payment of 110% of the allocated loan amount, applicable prepayment premium or yield maintenance, a minimum 10.0% post-release debt yield, no default, and a cumulative $26.87 million release cap across the pool.
deals.proximityHighways: Dual pylon signage on the Berlin Turnpike / Wilbur Cross Highway (14,000 VPD) and Deming Road (10,000 VPD), a primary retail corridor in Hartford County.
deals.retailCotenants: Competing and complementary retail in the immediate corridor includes a Target, Webster Square Shopping Center and Newington Fair Shopping Center. Hartford is approximately 15 miles north.

marketDemographics.source: Project Evergreen property OM (CBRE), Demographics page - 2025 current-year estimates
marketDemographics.note: OM also publishes a True Trade Area beyond 5 miles: 218,384 population, $119,939 average household income, 207,092 daytime population. This is the most affluent trade area in the Project Evergreen portfolio - roughly $119,000 average household income across every ring versus a $87,200 portfolio average. Population is essentially flat (0.01% annual growth at 5 miles) but households are growing 0.41% annually and income is projected to rise about 12% by 2030.

deals.notes: Brickyard Plaza is a 227,598 SF, 96.5%-leased community center on approximately 38.5 acres fronting the Berlin Turnpike in Berlin, Connecticut, built in 1990 and renovated in 2011. Home Depot has anchored the center since 1990 and occupies 103,003 SF, 45% of the GLA and 39% of total revenue, alongside Kohl's (58,966 SF), Michaels (21,429 SF) and PetSmart (20,405 SF) - four national credit anchors that together hold 90% of the building and give the center an unusually institutional income profile for this portfolio. In-place base rent from the 9/1/2026 rent roll is $2,015,885, or $9.18 PSF on occupied space, and CBRE's in-place pro-forma NOI is $1,852,162 on $2,831,819 of effective gross revenue. The trade area is the strongest in the portfolio by a wide margin: 170,825 residents within five miles at roughly $119,000 average household income and 218,384 across the true trade area, drawing 1.8 million annual visits with Michaels ranking in the 81st percentile of its chain nationally. The offsetting reality is that this credit quality is bought with rent that is locked cheap and long. Home Depot at $7.20, Kohl's at $7.00 and PetSmart at $11.67 all sit below CBRE's market rents, but Kohl's alone holds eight five-year options running to 2073 and Home Depot three to 2043, so almost none of the 10.15% below-market gap is capturable - it is durable, sticky income rather than upside. What a buyer is actually underwriting is a dense web of co-tenancy and go-dark rights layered on top of that concentration: Kohl's has NO continuous operating covenant and may go dark on 20 days' notice with rent continuing and no landlord recapture; PetSmart's rent halves if Kohl's stops operating; Michaels drops to alternative rent of 3% of gross sales if the anchor premises fall below an operating anchor or 70% occupancy; and Supercuts gets reduced rent and a termination right if either Home Depot or Kohl's permanently closes. Add real estate taxes running $2.45 PSF - $532,344 in 2025, 56% of the entire operating expense load and the highest tax burden in the portfolio - and Connecticut's revaluation cycle becomes a live underwriting item. The 8,045 SF vacancy is the former Imperial Buffet, which was doing $1.64 million in sales in 2024 on a lease that ran to October 2028 and stopped reporting mid-2025; understanding why a healthy tenant left four years early is a first-order diligence question.
keyAssumptions: SOURCES: roster built from the WHLR MRI rent roll dated 9/1/2026 (authoritative for current tenant, suite, SF, rent, dates and contractual steps); options, recovery methods, CAM caps, co-tenancy, go-dark and relocation clauses from the CBRE Argus model Project Evergreen_CT_Brickyard Plaza (FINAL).xlsx; reported tenant sales and occupancy costs from the WHLR 4-Year Sales Report for December 2025; historical income and expense from the WHLR income statement for the 12 months ended December 2025 (entity 0205, Cedar Brickyard, LLC); demographics, traffic counts, parking count, Placer.ai visitation and property description from the property OM; portfolio debt terms from the Project Evergreen portfolio OM (CBRE, data as of 8/26/2026).

ROSTER TIE-OUT: 11 leases plus one vacant suite sum to 227,598 SF, exactly the rent roll's stated GLA (219,553 occupied, 8,045 vacant, 96.47% occupied). Monthly base rent sums to $167,990.46, exactly the roll's printed total; annualized = $2,015,885.

HEADLINE NOI BASIS: noi / effectiveGrossIncome / operatingExpenses are CBRE's published In-Place Pro-Forma for calendar 2027 ($2,831,819 EGR less $979,657 of operating expense = $1,852,162), which ties exactly and is the basis behind the OM's stated in-place NOI. The VDR portfolio table rounds this to $1,850,000.

RECOVERIES BASIS: nnnRecoveries of $781,173 and the per-tenant expenseReimbursements are CBRE's in-place figures and combine BOTH the reimbursement line ($241,249) and the separately-billed real estate tax recovery ($539,923). The rent roll's monthly cost-recovery column totals only $249,260 annualized because Connecticut real estate taxes are billed annually rather than monthly - using the roll figure alone would understate true recoveries by roughly $532,000.

GPR RECONCILIATION: grossPotentialRent of $2,015,885 is the 9/1/2026 roll's in-place base rent and ties to the roster. CBRE's in-place pro-forma base rent of $2,039,840 is $23,955 higher because it runs contractual steps landing during calendar 2027 (PetSmart, Paragon, Luxury Nails, India Grocers and Shayona all step up between Nov-2026 and Jun-2027). CBRE's separate Gross Potential Rent line of $2,176,605 is higher still because it prices the vacant suite at market.

ACTUAL vs IN-PLACE: the owner's YE-2025 income statement shows actual NOI of $1,795,420 on $2,753,867 of total income and $958,448 of operating expense. The 2025 actuals are depressed by the Imperial Buffet vacancy and include a $140,527 negative prior-year tax true-up. CBRE's $979,657 in-place expense load is normalized to the 2026 budget with non-recoverable ownership-specific costs removed at $0.05 PSF and management fee modeled at 3.0% of EGR.

ACREAGE CONFLICT - VERIFY: the property OM states approximately 38.47 acres; the VDR portfolio table states 40.43 acres. lotSizeAcres carries the OM figure. Confirm against the survey before relying on either.

PETSMART TERM: the rent roll shows PetSmart's current lease expiring 1/31/2027 AND a follow-on lease for the same 20,405 SF running 2/1/2027 to 1/31/2032 under New Leases, so leaseExpiry carries 1/31/2032. CBRE describes the same extension as an assumed option exercise at $12.83 PSF. The roster holds the current $11.67 PSF contract rent so base rent ties to the roll, with the February 2027 step recorded in the rent schedule.

LUXURY NAILS TERM - VERIFY: the rent roll shows a contractual expiry of 10/31/2027. CBRE's model and the OM site plan both show October 2032, because CBRE assumes the tenant exercises a five-year option at $24.28 PSF. leaseExpiry carries the roll's contractual 10/31/2027 date with the option recorded separately. Given this tenant's reported occupancy cost, the option should not be treated as certain.
NO PRICING: the portfolio is marketed unpriced, so askingPrice, capRate and pricePerSF are null rather than estimated.

SALES BASIS: salesPSF and occupancyCost are calendar 2024, the most recent COMPLETE year in the WHLR 4-Year Sales Report. Calendar 2025 in that report is materially incomplete - several tenants show zero for four or more months - so using it would understate sales and overstate occupancy cost. Only three tenants report sales; the four anchors do not. Upload the sales report through the app's sales-report import to build the full trend history.

PLANET AID: a 0 SF donation-bin license paying $300 per month is carried as an ordinary tenant (NOT marked NAP) because its rent is inside the rent roll's base-rent total. The license runs to 2/28/2027.

LEASE CLAUSES ARE OM-SOURCED, NOT ABSTRACTED: the co-tenancy, go-dark, CAM-cap and relocation terms recorded in tenant notes come from CBRE's Argus lease summaries, not from executed lease documents. They are unverified and should be confirmed against the leases in diligence before being relied on.

redFlags.description: Kohl's can go dark at will with no landlord remedy - the lease has NO continuous operating covenant. Kohl's may cease operating at any time on 20 days' written notice, rent continues, and the landlord has NO recapture right. Kohl's is 58,966 SF (25.9% of GLA) at $7.00 PSF with eight five-year options running to January 2073. A dark Kohl's would keep paying but would trip PetSmart's 50% rent reduction, put Michaels into alternative rent, and give Supercuts a termination right - while leaving the landlord unable to re-tenant the box for up to 47 years.

Layered co-tenancy exposure keyed to the anchors. PetSmart (20,405 SF): if Kohl's or a comparable replacement ceases operating, base rent is reduced 50%; after 365 days PetSmart must within 30 days either terminate or resume full rent. Michaels (21,429 SF): if the anchor premises are not open and operated by an Anchor Tenant, or occupancy falls below 70%, and the failure persists 120 days, minimum rent abates and Michaels pays alternative rent of 3% of gross sales capped at minimum rent; after 12 months Michaels may terminate. Supercuts: if Home Depot OR Kohl's permanently ceases and is not replaced by a qualified national or regional tenant occupying 70% of the dark space within 60 days, reduced rent applies for up to 6 months and then Supercuts may terminate. Kohl's own co-tenancy is an occupancy test: if less than 130,000 SF of the center is open for 90 consecutive days, Kohl's may cut fixed rent 50% or terminate. These are OM-sourced summaries - confirm each against the executed lease.

Anchor concentration - Home Depot alone is 45% of GLA and 39% of total revenue, and the top four tenants are 90% of the building. Home Depot's lease expires 1/31/2028, roughly 12 months after a 2027 closing, with three five-year options at $7.64, $8.09 and $8.58 PSF. Home Depot also holds a go-dark recapture trigger cutting the other way: if it ceases operations for 90 consecutive days or gives notice of permanent closure, the LANDLORD may terminate within 120 days. There is very little income diversification to absorb an anchor loss.

Real estate taxes of $532,344 in 2025 - $2.45 PSF, 56% of the entire operating expense load and by far the highest tax burden in the portfolio. CBRE explicitly did NOT reassess taxes and modeled them at 2026 budgeted amounts, stating it is the investor's responsibility to reassess. Connecticut municipalities revalue on a five-year cycle; a sale at a materially higher basis than the current assessment would flow straight through NOI. Pull Berlin's current grand list, revaluation year and mill rate before underwriting.

Imperial Buffet vacated four years early and nobody has explained why - the 8,045 SF vacant suite 004 was Imperial Buffet on a lease running to 10/31/2028. The tenant did $1,368,630 (2022), $1,538,472 (2023) and $1,643,782 (2024) in sales at a healthy 12-13% occupancy cost, then stopped reporting after June 2025. A tenant performing that well leaving four years early usually means a lease termination, a buyout, a default or a landlord recapture. Ask for the termination or surrender agreement and whether any termination fee was collected - and note CBRE names its vacant-space assumption Imperial Backfill and models re-leasing at $17.00 PSF starting January 2028, a full year of carry.

Luxury Nails & Spa reports an unsustainable occupancy cost - 2024 sales of $68,275 ($46.73 PSF) against roughly $44,128 of rent and recoveries is a 64.6% occupancy cost, and 2025 reporting is worse. Sales have fallen from $100,586 in 2023 to $68,275 in 2024. Either the tenant is materially underreporting sales or it cannot survive at this rent. The contractual lease expires 10/31/2027 and CBRE's model assumes the tenant exercises its option at a HIGHER rent of $24.28 PSF - an assumption the sales data does not support.

Shayona Foods occupancy cost of 23.6% - 2024 sales of $158,453 ($89.17 PSF) against $37,374 of rent and recoveries. High for a food operator, on a lease expiring 5/31/2028. Combined with Luxury Nails, two of the three sales-reporting small shops are stressed.

Widespread go-dark and recapture triggers among the small shops - Shayona Foods, Luxury Nails and India Grocers all carry continuous-operation covenants where going dark 30 or more consecutive days lets the landlord terminate or recapture, and Supercuts pays a $7,500 termination fee if it goes dark 60 days. These protect the landlord, but they also mean a soft-sales tenant that quietly closes converts to vacancy quickly rather than continuing to pay.

Three tenants hold landlord relocation rights (The UPS Store, Paragon Strength, Luxury Nails and Supercuts), and Kohl's premises are subject to a recorded REA. Neither is unusual, but both constrain redevelopment or re-merchandising of the center and should be read alongside the REA before any pad or reconfiguration plan is underwritten.

CAM caps limit recovery growth on four leases - PetSmart 5% non-cumulative, Supercuts 6% cumulative, The UPS Store 10% non-cumulative, India Grocers 3% non-cumulative, each excluding snow and ice removal, security and utilities. India Grocers' 3% non-cumulative cap is tight against a 3.0% expense growth assumption, and Connecticut snow costs ran $78,290 in 2025.

upsideItems.item: Lease up the 8,045 SF former Imperial Buffet space
upsideItems.detail: The only vacancy at the center, 3.5% of GLA. CBRE models a January 2028 backfill at $17.00 PSF NNN on a 5-year term with $25.00 PSF of TI and 6% commissions - roughly $137,000 of incremental base rent plus recoveries. A restaurant-improved 8,045 SF box on the Berlin Turnpike in a $119,000-income trade area should lease; the question is timing and whether the Imperial departure signals something about the space itself.

Unlike the anchors, the shop leases roll without long option chains. Supercuts ($29.00 vs $30.00 market) and The UPS Store ($27.68 vs $28.00) hold NO renewal options and expire in 2028 and 2029; Shayona and India Grocers roll in 2028 with single options. CBRE marks shop space at $15.00 to $30.00 PSF with 3% annual growth. This is where the portfolio's mark-to-market thesis is actually true at this asset.

upsideItems.item: Best trade area in the portfolio
upsideItems.detail: 170,825 residents within five miles at $119,043 average household income, 218,384 across the true trade area at $119,939, and 207,092 daytime population - roughly 37% above the portfolio's $87,200 average income. Households are growing 0.41% annually within five miles and the 1-mile ring is growing 3.04% annually. Under the demographics-to-rent lens this location supports both above-average rent and a tighter going-in cap than the portfolio average, and it materially deepens the pool of replacement tenants if an anchor does roll.

1.8 million annual visits (TTM, Placer.ai), with Michaels ranking in the 81st percentile of its chain's foot traffic nationally - independent evidence the anchors are performing, not just occupying. Michaels also renewed into a fresh term effective March 2026, which is a tenant voting with its own capital.

$14,749,120 of allocated Guggenheim debt at 5.25% fixed, interest-only into 2027 and maturing November 2032, assumable by a buyer. Whether this is genuinely accretive depends on where financing prices at closing, and the release mechanics (110% of allocated loan amount, 10% minimum post-release debt yield, $26.87M cumulative pool release cap) constrain selling this asset separately from the other eight in the pool.

CBRE projects 3.16% five-year and 2.53% ten-year NOI CAGR driven mostly by contractual bumps across a credit roster rather than speculative lease-up - NOI rises from $1,852,162 to $2,053,570 in 2028 (10.9%) largely on the PetSmart extension and shop steps already signed.

tenants.name: Home Depot
tenants.rentSchedule: Flat at $7.20 PSF ($61,833.33/month) through 1/31/2028 - no contractual increases in the current term.
tenants.rentBumps: None in current term; approximately 6% at each option.
tenants.assumptionNote: Rent roll entity HOME DEPOT #6203. Anchoring the center since January 1990 - 36 years of tenure. 45.3% of GLA and 39.0% of total revenue, the largest single-tenant concentration in the portfolio. GO-DARK / LANDLORD RECAPTURE: if tenant ceases operations for 90 or more consecutive days (excluding casualty, condemnation and acts of God) or gives notice of permanent closure, LANDLORD may terminate the lease within 120 days. Rent of $7.20 PSF is roughly 10% below CBRE's $8.00 PSF market rent, but the option chain runs to January 2043 at a maximum of $8.58 PSF - this below-market rent is locked and secure, not capturable mark-to-market. Current term expires roughly 12 months after a 2027 closing; CBRE assumes the first option is exercised. Clause detail is OM-sourced and unverified against the executed lease.

tenants.name: Kohl's
tenants.reimbursementMethod: Custom Kohl's recovery schedule - fixed CAM contribution
tenants.rentSchedule: Flat at $7.00 PSF ($34,396.83/month) through 1/31/2033. The rent roll shows only a nominal fixed CAM escalation of roughly $2/month each January from 2027 through 2033.
tenants.rentBumps: None in current term; 10% at each option.
tenants.assumptionNote: Rent roll entity KOHL'S #1448. 25.9% of GLA and 19.8% of revenue. GO DARK - NO OPERATING COVENANT: Kohl's may operate as a Kohl's or any zoning-permitted use (subject to Exhibit J exclusives and the recorded REA); there is NO continuous operating covenant, tenant may go dark at any time on 20 days' prior written notice with rent continuing, and the LANDLORD HAS NO RECAPTURE RIGHT. CO-TENANCY (Kohl's as beneficiary): if less than 130,000 SF of the center excluding outparcels and Kohl's own building is open for 90 or more consecutive days (excluding casualty, condemnation, remodeling, major repairs and labor action), Kohl's may after notice and a 30-day cure either cut fixed rent 50% until cured or terminate, with the termination right vesting only one year after the failure. Premises subject to a recorded REA. Rent of $7.00 PSF is 22% below CBRE's $9.00 PSF market rent, but with options to 2073 that gap is permanently locked - secure income, never capturable. Clause detail is OM-sourced and unverified against the executed lease. Kohl's fixed CAM contribution of roughly $2,299/year means this tenant contributes almost nothing toward controllable operating costs.

tenants.name: Michaels
tenants.rentSchedule: Flat at $16.50 PSF ($29,464.88/month) through 2/28/2031 - no contractual increases in the current term.
tenants.rentBumps: None in current term; approximately 9% at each option.
tenants.assumptionNote: Rent roll entity MICHAELS #5072. Original occupancy March 2015; renewed into a fresh five-year term effective 3/1/2026 - a tenant committing its own capital, and the strongest recent leasing signal at the center. Placer.ai ranks this store in the 81st percentile of Michaels' chain foot traffic. At $16.50 versus CBRE's $17.00 PSF market rent this lease is essentially at market. CO-TENANCY: the Anchor Premises per Exhibit B must be open and operated by an Anchor Tenant (defined tenants, or 70%-plus occupancy). If the failure persists 120 days, minimum rent abates and tenant pays Alternative Rent of 3% of gross sales capped at minimum rent. If failure continues 12 months, tenant may terminate within 30 days; if it does not, landlord may demand tenant either terminate or resume full rent (90-day waiver). Tenant still owes its pro rata share of taxes and CAM during Alternative Rent. GO-DARK / RECAPTURE: if tenant goes dark 180 or more consecutive days, landlord may terminate on 30 days' notice and tenant reimburses unamortized brokerage commissions; the right does not vest if tenant reopens, is negotiating an assignment or sublease, or a subtenant opens within 150 days. Excludes remodeling, casualty, condemnation and uncontrollable events. Clause detail is OM-sourced and unverified.

tenants.reimbursementMethod: Custom PetSmart recovery schedule; 5% non-cumulative CAM cap excluding snow and ice removal, security and utilities
tenants.rentSchedule: 2/1/2027 step to $12.83 PSF ($261,796/year, +9.94%). Flat thereafter through 1/31/2032.

tenants.assumptionNote: Rent roll entity PETSMART #2718. The roll shows the current term expiring 1/31/2027 and a follow-on lease for the same premises running 2/1/2027 to 1/31/2032 under New Leases; CBRE describes the same extension as an assumed five-year option exercise at $12.83 PSF. Carried at the current $11.67 PSF contract rent with the February 2027 step in the rent schedule, so base rent ties to the roll. CO-TENANCY: if Kohl's or a comparable replacement ceases operating (excluding temporary closures up to 180 days for casualty, condemnation or remodeling), base rent is reduced 50%. If the failure continues 365 days, tenant must within 30 days of landlord notice either terminate (effective in 60 days) or resume full rent; failure to elect waives termination. This is a direct, single-anchor dependency on Kohl's - and Kohl's has no operating covenant. GO-DARK: if tenant goes dark 180 or more consecutive days (excluding casualty, condemnation, remodeling), landlord may terminate on 90 days' notice unless tenant or an assignee reopens or is diligently preparing to reopen within 90 days. Clause detail is OM-sourced and unverified.

tenants.name: Supercuts
tenants.reimbursementMethod: Custom Supercuts recovery schedule; 6% cumulative CAM cap excluding snow and ice removal, security and utilities
tenants.assumptionNote: Original occupancy August 2013, roughly 13 years of tenure. At $29.00 versus CBRE's $30.00 PSF market rent, essentially at market, with NO renewal options - genuinely open at the 8/31/2028 expiry. CO-TENANCY: if Home Depot OR Kohl's permanently ceases operating and landlord does not replace with a Qualified Replacement (a national or regional tenant occupying 70% or more of the dark space) within 60 days of tenant notice (excluding remodeling up to 180 days and casualty), tenant if open and not in default pays Reduced Rent until replacement or 6 months, whichever comes first.
